legal_sources.citation: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30, Arts. 1-2 only (which of Art. 3(3)(d)-(f) apply, and the exemptions); the rest of the regulation and the harmonised standards are not modelled

questions.label: Is this amateur radio equipment that is not made available on the market (a kit for radio amateurs to assemble, or equipment they build or modify for their own use)?
questions.guidance: Commercially available amateur radio equipment is in scope. The exclusion covers kits and self-built or self-modified equipment used by licensed radio amateurs.

questions.label: Is this a custom-built evaluation kit for professionals, used solely at research and development facilities?
Is the product on-board equipment for electronic road toll systems under Directive (EU) 2019/520?
Which of these categories is the product?
questions.guidance: These are the categories of radio equipment covered by the common charger rules. A product in none of them answers 'None of these'.

questions.label: Can the product's battery be recharged through a cable?
Does wired charging need more than 5 V, more than 3 A or more than 15 W?
Is the product a mobile phone with the features of a handheld computer (a smartphone)?
Have you applied, in full, harmonised standards that cover effective and efficient use of radio spectrum (Article 3(2)) for this product?
questions.guidance: Only standards whose references are published in the Official Journal under the RED give a presumption of conformity. If you applied them only partly, or none exists for your radio technology, a notified body must be involved. See the Blue Guide, sections 4.1.2 and 5.1.

questions.label: Have you applied, in full, harmonised standards for every Article 3(3) requirement that applies to the product (for network protection, privacy and fraud: EN 18031-1, -2 or -3, without the options the Official Journal citation restricts)?
questions.guidance: The EN 18031 series is cited with restrictions: where the standard lets you choose an option that the citation excludes (for example, letting the user skip setting a password), the standard no longer gives a presumption of conformity and a notified body must be involved.

finding_rules.message: Harmonised standards were not applied in full for Article 3(2) or for the Article 3(3) requirements that apply: a notified body must be involved (modules B+C or H).
Radio hardware is present but disabled; enabling it by update or option makes the product radio equipment and requires re-assessment.
A radio that cannot emit or receive is not treated as radio equipment; if it is made operable again, the RED applies.
The user can switch the radio on, so the product is radio equipment even when shipped with it off.
An importer or distributor that places the product under its own name or modifies it in a way that may affect compliance has the manufacturer's obligations.
The RED has no open-source steward role: whoever places the radio equipment on the market is its manufacturer or importer.
The same default password on every unit does not meet the network, privacy and fraud protection requirements, and the EN 18031 citation excludes it.
Updates installed without verifying their authenticity let an attacker replace the software.
Without an update mechanism, vulnerabilities found after placing on the market cannot be fixed in the field; justify it in the risk assessment.
Personal data on some external channels is not protected; justify it in the risk assessment or encrypt it.

The Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) also applies to radio equipment with a data connection, including one that only connects locally, unless one of its exclusions applies; assess the product with the EU CRA package too. Its vulnerability and incident reporting duties (Art. 14) apply from 11 September 2026, also to products already on the market; the other requirements apply from 11 December 2027, and to products placed earlier only after a substantial modification.

Document an analysis and assessment of the risks. Annex V does not list it as a separate item, but the conformity assessment must cover the safety objectives of Art. 3(1)(a) (Art. 17(1)), and for EU-type examination the technical documentation must include it (Annex III, Module B, point 3(c)).
finding_rules.ref: Art. 17(1), Art. 21; Annex III, Module B, point 3(c)

finding_rules.message: Complete the technical documentation before placing the product on the market.
Mark the electrical ratings and other essential characteristics on the equipment, or in an accompanying document.
Draw up the EU declaration of conformity before placing the product on the market.
Affix the CE marking before placing the product on the market.
Mark a type, batch or serial number and the manufacturer's name and postal address on the units, or on the packaging or documents where that is not possible.
Supply instructions and safety information in a language easily understood by users in every Member State where the product is sold.
Check the CE marking, the instructions and safety information and the identification of the manufacturer and importer before supplying the product.

Art. 3(3)(d), (e) and (f) are switched on by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30. This package models only its Arts. 1-2: which of the three requirements apply to the product and the exemptions. It is an own summary and has not been legally reviewed, so it does not show that the delegated regulation is fully met. Check the product against the regulation itself and the cited harmonised standards.
